vendor_accounts.description: Every vendor account that more than one environment calls has one row here (#1520). A row holds the limits of the vendor, each with its evidence, and the percent of each environment. The share of a limit is amount x percent // 100 (integer floor), in the window of the limit. The shares of the environments never sum past the amount. A share of 0 is not an error: the contract loads and the gate refuses the call. A limit with the evidence kind self_imposed is our own pace. The gate enforces it and never divides it. A limit with no amount (none_published, not_known) is shown and never invented. An environment that this table does not name (local, CI) gets the whole figure of a host_ip account and no call to any other account. The gate enforces the shares of twelvedata, sec_edgar and openfigi now, and the self_imposed paces of yahoo, nasdaq_index and us_treasury. It does not enforce moomoo_opend yet: moomoo calls skip the gate until step 2 of #1520, and the K-line stock quota is still a constant of moomoo_ledger.py. It does not enforce model_plan: the pace of the model seat stays in model_seat.environments until step 5 of #1520. The default percent 20/20/60 is owner decision D4 of 2026-10-26. The Twelve Data override 0/40/60 and the moomoo shares 6/6/18 are working choices of 2026-10-27, not owner approval.

run_time_bounds.description: The maximum runtime of every deployed Dagster job (#1442). Bound = margin x the longest successful run over all measured environments, and never below floor_minutes. A job that never ran takes live_tick_fit at the largest listing count of its tick. The run launcher writes the bound to the run tag dagster/max_runtime. The run monitor fails a run that exceeds its bound. The bound starts from the longest success, not from p95: p95 x 2 ends real successes (staging head_reports_pipeline: p95 5.3 min, longest success 22.5 min). The floor keeps scheduler jitter and lock waits from ending a short job; it is five run-monitor polls of 2 minutes.

code_server_capacity.description: The memory that the Dagster code server container gives to its processes, and the run limit of dagster.yaml (#1467). Every run executes inside the code server container, in the same cgroup as the gRPC server. The queue admits concurrent_runs runs (at least 2: a run that waits for other runs holds a slot). The processes may hold the share UTILIZATION_CEILING of the ceiling (the owner rule of #1418, one constant in environment_contract.py). The server holds server_mib = ceil(measured.grpc_server_hwm_mib x (1 + server_margin)). The budget of one run process is run_mib = floor((usable_mib - server_processes x server_mib) / (concurrent_runs x processes_per_run)). It is a decision, not a measurement. Tests hold dagster.yaml equal to concurrent_runs and the deployed jobs to processes_per_run. The nightly verdict runtime_shape reads the real memory.max, memory.peak and oom_kill of the container and every process size. It fails when the ceiling is lower than declared here, when the peak of a container rises above the usable share of memory.max, when a process is larger than the server or run budget, when the swap peak rises while the container is at memory.max, or when a kill or an unplanned restart is seen. A sensor keeps the counters of containers that a deploy replaced.
code_server_capacity.ceiling_source: infra2 truealpha/truealpha/20.data_engine/compose.yaml, x-dagster-service mem_limit, one value for staging and production (infra2#1342)

measured.method: Server: VmHWM of /proc/1/status in the code server container (docker exec, read only), 13 hours after its start. server_margin is 10% for growth (the same reading was 229.5 MiB on 2026-10-20 and 211.5 MiB for a fresh server in a Linux container). Fresh import: VmHWM of /proc/self/status of a fresh interpreter that imports data_engine.dagster_defs, in a Linux container with the image layout (uv sync --frozen --no-dev --no-editable). Working run: the sensor (every 30 s) sampled the boot burst of the deploy of v0.2.35 on staging, 2026-10-21 06:41-06:46 UTC, when canary_live_pipeline and topt_live_pipeline ran together; the largest VmHWM of any process except the code server in that container was 384.4 MiB (dagster.kvs, key truealpha/runtime_shape/tracker, field largest_process). The container peak counts page cache and kernel memory, and the process peaks need not fall at the same moment, so no size per run is derived from it. The runtime_shape verdict measures the largest process of every sample and goes red above run_mib. Staging runs the TOPT universe only; production sizes come from its first nights.

model_seat.description: The limits of the model provider seat (#1444). All environments call one coding-plan account, and other users of that account share its rate limit. When the account is over its limit, it answers HTTP 429 with provider code 1302. Every model call passes one retry policy: the extraction path and the nightly key probe. A call retries only on a transient answer. A transient answer is HTTP 429 without a terminal provider code, or any answer with a transient provider code. The wait before retry n is min(initial_backoff_seconds x backoff_factor^(n-1), max_backoff_seconds), plus a random extra of at most jitter_percent. The random extra only lengthens the wait, so the waits sum to at least min_total_wait_seconds. A call stops after max_attempts attempts, or when the next wait would pass deadline_seconds since the first attempt. The wait of an attempt for the per-minute window also counts against that deadline. A call lasts at most deadline_seconds plus the timeout of one attempt. The wait for a concurrency slot counts against the deadline too. The timeout of an attempt is a socket timeout: it limits each socket operation, not the whole response. Each attempt is one ledger row. Each environment starts at most calls_per_minute attempts per minute and runs at most max_concurrent_calls attempts at one time. The limit is per environment because the account is shared. The probe starts at probe.hour_utc plus probe_offset_minutes of its environment, up to launch_margin_seconds late (the probe of production was seen 40 s late on 2026-10-21). The probe call uses attempt_timeout_seconds as its attempt timeout. Probe slots of two environments stay at least probe.slot_minutes apart. slot_minutes holds the deadline, one attempt and the launch margin, so the retries of one probe never meet the probe of another environment. Each environment names the decoding version of its model request (decoding_version, default v1; the versions are defined in data_engine.sources.model_decoding). Production moves to another version only with a production release that the owner approves. An environment that is not listed (dev, ci) has no pacing limit, the probe offset 0 and the default decoding version.
